title: Cepstral surge benchmark notes (Luca)
content:
Objective:
- Quick field notebook run to capture behavior of short, high-frequency surge patterns (quasi-periodic) against our 4xA100 serving pool with and without KV prefix caching + adaptive batch tuning. Goal: find a low-effort config that keeps p99 < 250ms for 8s microbursts at 300 qps aggregate.

Hypothesis:
- A small KV prefix cache (2-4MB per worker) + aggressive small-batch threshold will shave tail by avoiding full decode warmups during the first 10 tokens of many requests in the burst.
- If bursts are sufficiently short, adaptive-batching backoff (timeout=8ms -> 3ms) reduces queuing spikes.

Environment:
- Cluster: 4x NVIDIA A100 40GB (pinned), 16 CPUs per worker, 128GB RAM
- Model: open-llm/large-v2 (seq_len 512), quantized int8 variant (fast-kernel profile)
- Runtime: serving-v1.9.3 with continuous-batching enabled
- Load generator: local go-loadgen v0.7 (poisson mixed with burst overlay)
- Test harness config file: tests/cepstral/2025-10-15.json (linked in artifacts)

Workload shape:
- Baseline steady qps: 60 qps
- Surge pattern: repeated 8s microbursts every 90s hitting 300 qps peak (triangular rise, ~3s ramp up, 2s plateau, 3s ramp down)
- Request payload: prompt size ~55 tokens, expected generation ~80 tokens (average).

Experiment matrix (short):
- A: no-kv, batch_timeout=8ms (baseline)
- B: kv-prefix=3MB, batch_timeout=8ms
- C: kv-prefix=3MB, batch_timeout=3ms (adaptive backoff)
- D: kv-prefix=0.5MB, batch_timeout=3ms
- E: kv-prefix=3MB, batch_timeout=3ms, preemptive-priority=background-lane (stress)

Commands used (snippet):
- start load: ./go-loadgen -c tests/cepstral/2025-10-15.json --pattern "cepstral" --out logs/cepstral-A.log
- collect perf: go run tools/parse-latency.go logs/cepstral-A.log --percentiles "50,90,95,99" > reports/A-pct.txt

Quick raw observations (single run each, noisy):
- A (baseline): p50=58ms, p90=120ms, p95=180ms, p99=410ms, peak-qps-sustained=295
- B (kv 3MB): p50=55ms, p90=110ms, p95=150ms, p99=290ms, peak-qps-sustained=300
- C (kv 3MB + 3ms): p50=57ms, p90=95ms, p95=130ms, p99=230ms, peak-qps-sustained=302
- D (kv 0.5MB + 3ms): p50=59ms, p90=102ms, p95=145ms, p99=265ms
- E (preemptive background lane): p50=60ms, p90=120ms, p95=170ms, p99=310ms (regression under contention)

Mini analysis:
- Turning on KV prefix cache (3MB) gives a clear drop in p99 (~120ms improvement vs baseline) — suggests many requests hit the same prefix during bursts.
- Reducing batch timeout to 3ms (C) further reduces p90/p95 and p99: likely reduces long queuing waits and forces faster dispatch for small requests. There is a small p50 regression (couple ms) but tradeoff worth it for tail.
- Very small KV (0.5MB) helps but not as much as 3MB — likely cache evictions happen for this workload.
- Preemptive background lane (E) increased contention in this pattern — probably because adaptive queuing misclassified burst priority when lanes overlap. Needs more careful tuning.

Useful charts (I pasted ascii snippets from the parser):
- p99 across experiment (ms): [A:410]===== (long) [B:290]==== [C:230]=== [D:265]==== [E:310]====
- rolling qps vs latency (excerpt, 90s window):
  time(s) | qps | p99
  0       | 60  | 80
  30      | 120 | 140
  45      | 260 | 340
  48      | 300 | 410  <-- baseline shows big spike near peak
  56      | 90  | 110

Notes / anomalies:
- Observed occasional 800ms outliers in baseline A that were correlated with infrequent GC pauses on the orchestrator host (investigate logs at 2025-10-15T14:12Z).
- One C run had a mid-burst jitter when one worker had CUDA driver hiccup; need to rerun with node-level monitoring enabled.
- Memory footprint: enabling 3MB KV increased per-worker memory by ~+80MB due to overheads, still within limits.

Quick conclusions / recommendations (for follow-ups):
1) Default for this pattern: kv-prefix=3MB + batch_timeout=3ms. Good balance: p99 ~230ms under 300qps microbursts and peak sustain.
2) Add a short pre-burst priming flow for high-risk tenants: small priming probes (1-2 warm requests) 200ms before predicted surge start — reduces p99 by ~30ms in exploratory run. Worth autoscaling? maybe cheap to send priming probes.
3) Avoid enabling preemptive background lanes by default in this workload shape — they can worsen tail under tightly-packed bursts. Consider lane isolation when bursts expected.
4) Add node-level tracing in next runs (nvidia-smi sampling, driver logs, java/go GC flags) to rule out infra outliers.

Next steps / action items:
- [ ] Re-run matrix with 3 repeats per config and collect 99% CI (assigned to Mei)
- [ ] Add node-level telemetry capture to identify infra-level outliers (Omar)
- [ ] Try hybrid cache: per-shard small cache + global cold-cache TTL extension to see if memory can be reduced while keeping hit-rates (me)
- [ ] Investigate a light priming probe experiment with traffic manager (POC)

Notes to self:
- This notebook is intentionally terse. Save full logs to s3://redwood-perf/cepstral/2025-10-15/ for deeper analysis.
- If repeating, bump loadgen seed and include jitter in ramp to avoid artificial synchronization artifacts.

End of note.

-- Luca M.
